answer: Like a meadow, the network scatters verification like pollen: each identity's work is checked by neighbors, and honest pollen drifts far. Farm identities only pollinate each other, so their pollen never leaves their own orchard - a closed loop, easy to spot. The network also shifts the ground like a dune, moving the checks each season, so each identity must keep proving itself. Honest identities move with the sand; farm sockpuppets sit in one spot and get buried when the dune shifts. To survive, a farm must pollinate the whole meadow for every sockpuppet - as expensive as honest work.
